# OpenC 1.0.1

This Windows x86-64 Hosted release completes the SH-27 compiler-throughput and
incremental-build work. Core and Hosted language editions remain 1.0.

- Checked local integer updates use a compact native lowering plan. The
  original large-function corpus produces about 70% fewer intermediate
  instructions while preserving overflow and conversion checks.
- Two independent clean Windows runs certify all twenty original comparison
  ratios against pinned MSVC, Clang, DMD, and LDC. The separately restricted
  local host also passes both planned DMD runs at 1.05x/1.12x for large
  functions, below the unchanged 1.20x engineering target.
- Ordinary builds reuse validated native objects and frontend contributions.
  Cold, unchanged and edited compiler/application builds, malformed cache
  recovery, publication failures and four-project batches retain measured
  correctness and resource evidence.
- Deterministic standalone, source and editor packages contain the complete
  230-source compiler. Clean-profile editor, relocated package, 278-fixture
  conformance, Windows ABI and strict 20-generation closure checks pass.

The normal toolchain uses the first-party native compiler and linker without
D, C, Python, TinyCC, an external assembler or an external linker. External
Python/GitHub tools orchestrate release and differential evidence only.

`OpenC-1.0.1-SH27-evidence.zip` retains the raw hosted certificates and their
authenticated artifact receipts. `OpenC-Core-1.0-SHA256SUMS.txt` and the release
record identify all payloads. Published 1.0.0 assets remain immutable.
